summary.headline: A Slack app takes minutes to create. A commercial AI agent, though, needs its own Slack Marketplace listing: plan on 10 active pilot workspaces and a review of up to about 12 weeks. Until you're listed, new installs read history at 15 messages per minute, and the Real-time Search API and MCP server are unavailable.
summary.overview: Slack apps are self-serve: create one from a manifest, add Composio's redirect URI, and install it in your own workspace with no review. Since the May 2025 policy change, unlisted ('Activate Public Distribution') apps are meant for pilots. Slack's API Terms say commercial distribution, including a free app tied to a paid product, needs the Marketplace or a partner agreement. Unlisted apps also get 1 request per minute and 15 messages per call on conversations.history/replies for new installs, and cannot use the Real-time Search API or the Slack MCP server. Marketplace review requires 10 active workspaces kept for the whole review, AI disclosures, and justified, minimal scopes.
drivers: API Terms (effective 10 Oct 2025): commercial distribution requires the Marketplace Agreement or a partner agreement, and this covers templated custom apps too
Submission gate: at least 10 active, non-sandbox workspaces (back to 10 as of July 2026), kept through the whole review
Official review window: up to 10 business days preliminary plus up to 10 weeks functional; preliminary resubmissions reset the queue
Unlisted apps: conversations.history/replies at 1 request per minute and 15 objects for new installs; no Real-time Search API or MCP server

Enhanced review for agent-typical scopes (*:history, search:read.*, files:read); legacy search:read, identity.* and coded-workflow scopes make an app unsuitable, and admin.* is unlikely to be approved outside Slack's partner program
AI rules: no LLM training on Slack data, plus model, retention, tenancy and residency disclosures
summary.bestCase: Internal use only: an app in your own workspace connected to Composio in under an hour, with no review and full rate limits. Commercial: one vendor (Viktor) reports approval in two weeks, but only after a viral launch led Salesforce to prioritise its review; the same vendor calls 2-3 months typical.
summary.worstCase: The preliminary review returns the submission repeatedly (each resubmission resets the queue), then the functional review takes the full 10 weeks. Or the app is judged unsuitable, for example because it has no in-Slack functionality or relies on broad user *:history access. You stay unlisted, with the history clamp and no RTS/MCP. Dropping below 10 installed workspaces during review also stalls it.

paths.name: Slack Marketplace listing (commercial AI agent)

You pilot unlisted until at least 10 active workspaces have installed the app, then submit for review: up to 10 business days preliminary and up to 10 weeks functional, with a possible security review. Agent-specific scrutiny applies: AI disclosures, no LLM training, and an enhanced review for *:history, search:read.* and files:read.

composio.note: Composio manages OAuth apps for both the 'slack' toolkit (user token) and the 'slackbot' toolkit (posts as the bot; Composio says it also reads workspace-wide on behalf of the installing user), so you can prototype with no Slack app of your own. Composio says it 'is working on Marketplace review for the managed Slack app'. Until that is done, connections through the managed app follow unlisted-app rules: a 'not listed in the Slack Marketplace' warning, owner approval in restrictive workspaces, and, by inference from Slack's rules, the 15-message/1-per-minute history clamp for new installs and no access to the Real-time Search or MCP features. Consent also shows Composio rather than your brand. Bring your own app for your branding, a dedicated rate-limit quota (Slack counts limits per method, per workspace, per app, so the managed app's quota is shared with every other Composio-backed product connected to the same workspace), custom scopes, polling triggers faster than the managed 15-minute minimum, or a Marketplace listing under your name. oauth.refreshTokens: Only when token rotation is on. It is opt-in under OAuth & Permissions, or Published App Settings for Marketplace apps, and it cannot be turned off. Refresh with oauth.v2.access grant_type=refresh_token plus client_id and client_secret. Refresh tokens are single-use, so store the new one every time. Refreshing early is limited to 2 active tokens. Apps with PKCE enabled get refresh tokens that expire after 30 days. PKCE installs that redirect to a custom URI scheme always get rotating tokens.
oauth.tokenLifetime: Without rotation, bot (xoxb-) and user (xoxp-) tokens never expire; they end when revoked or the app is uninstalled. With rotation, access tokens (xoxe.xoxb-/xoxe.xoxp-) last 12 hours (expires_in 43200). Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes. App configuration tokens for the Manifest API last 12 hours.
oauth.redirectUris: HTTPS only. The redirect_uri must match, or be a subdirectory of, a Redirect URL saved under OAuth & Permissions; no '#' anchors. If several Redirect URLs are saved, send the same redirect_uri to both authorize and oauth.v2.access, or you get bad_redirect_uri. Without the parameter, the first saved URL is used. Custom URI schemes (myapp://) only work with PKCE enabled. With PKCE on, http://localhost is treated as a desktop redirect, and desktop redirects can't request bot scopes. No wildcard hosts are documented.
oauth.scopes: Granular scopes: bot scopes go in 'scope' and user scopes in 'user_scope', comma-separated, in the same authorize URL. Scopes add up across re-installs and can't be reduced without revoking the token. The x-oauth-scopes response header shows the current grant. Optional scopes (manifest bot_optional/user_optional, March 2026) let users decline non-core scopes. Sign in with Slack (openid) scopes can't be mixed with other user scopes. Once an app is published in the Marketplace, its scopes are locked until a re-review, and requesting unapproved scopes gives unapproved_scope.

requirements.detail: 'Commercially Distribute' covers direct charges, freemium, and free apps that connect to a paid product. It also covers custom apps or app templates you give to customers. requirements.title: At least 10 active workspaces before and during review
requirements.detail: Submissions are automatically blocked unless the app is installed on 10 or more workspaces used in the past 28 days; sandboxes don't count. The count must stay at 10 or more for the whole review. The guidelines' unsuitable list repeats this as apps 'installed on less than 10 active workspaces and have less than 10 weekly active users' (both conditions), so weekly active users is not a separate gate. requirements.title: Public landing and support pages

nuances.detail: Since 29 May 2025, new non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps, and new installs of existing ones, get conversations.history and conversations.replies at 1 request per minute and a maximum and default limit of 15. Internal and Marketplace apps keep Tier 3 (50+ requests per minute, limit up to about 1,000; the method page says a maximum of 999). Community testing reports the clamped call still returns ok:true with 15 messages and a next_cursor, and a second call within the minute returns ratelimited with Retry-After of about 60. For existing installs, Slack's own docs first scheduled the clamp for 2 September 2025, then moved it to 3 March 2026 (archived copies of the changelog and of the method page, the latter still saying so on 3 February 2026), and by 2 March 2026 changed the text to say existing installs will not be subject to the new limits, which current docs still say. Third-party posts describing a rollout to existing installs ending 3 March 2026 reflect that superseded plan (see openQuestions).

It works for prototyping but not for a production agent that reads a lot.

evidence.note: Composio is working on Marketplace review for the managed Slack app

nuances.title: Real-time Search API and Slack MCP server: Marketplace or internal apps only
nuances.detail: Both are built for LLM and agent use. Real-time Search searches as the user, without you storing the data, using the granular search:read.public/.private/.im/.mpim/.files/.users scopes. The Slack MCP server is at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp over Streamable HTTP, with no SSE and no dynamic client registration, and needs a registered Slack app with a fixed app ID. Neither is available to unlisted distributed apps. Natural-language (semantic) RTS queries only work on workspaces whose plan includes Slack AI Search, and a listed app that offers semantic search must tell users a Business+ or Enterprise+ plan is required; check with assistant.search.info.

evidence.note: No unlisted distributed apps allowed; semantic search is available only on workspaces within plans that include Slack AI Search

nuances.title: Handing customers a manifest doesn't avoid the Marketplace

Slack's terms apply the commercial-distribution restrictions 'regardless of whether you publish an off-the-shelf Application or you provide customers with a custom Application or Application template'. The only stated exception is an app built for a single third party.

nuances.title: Scope posture reviewers apply to agents
nuances.detail: Bot scopes should be the default, and user scopes are only accepted where the action must come from the user. Broad user-token *:history is 'unlikely' to be approved without a Real-time Search or MCP use case. search:read.*, *:history, files:read and canvases:read trigger an enhanced review, as do user-token groups:write, groups:write.invites and mpim:write, conversations.connect:write and admin.*. Automation-platform apps must limit installs to paid Slack plans (check with team.billing:read) and must not request user *:history or files:read to collect message or file data. Free-plan workspaces have 90 days of history, and the app must not expose anything older.

nuances.title: Token rotation and PKCE are one-way switches

PKCE became self-serve on 30 March 2026, but enabling it makes the app a public client (a one-way switch that only Slack support can undo), gives all its refresh tokens a 30-day expiry, and blocks bot scopes on desktop (custom-scheme or localhost) redirects. nuances.title: Slack's token errors arrive as HTTP 200

nuances.title: Scopes add up and are locked after listing

artifacts.title: Production Slack app manifest for an AI agent connected through Composio
artifacts.content:
# Production manifest for <YOUR_APP_NAME> (AI agent connected through Composio)
# Paste into api.slack.com/apps -> Create New App -> From a manifest.
# Replace every <PLACEHOLDER>. Remove any scope your shipped features do not use.
display_information:
  name: <YOUR_APP_NAME>          # max 35 characters
  description: <10 words or fewer, e.g. "Ask <YOUR_PRODUCT> to summarize and act on your work">
  background_color: "#1d1c1d"
  long_description: >-           # 174-4000 characters or the manifest is rejected
    <YOUR_APP_NAME> connects Slack to <YOUR_PRODUCT>, an AI assistant that ...
    AI-generated answers can be inaccurate; review them before acting.
    Slack data is never used to train AI models.
features:
  app_home:
    home_tab_enabled: true        # onboarding, help, pricing, support link
    messages_tab_enabled: true
    messages_tab_read_only_enabled: false
  bot_user:
    display_name: <YOUR_APP_NAME>
    always_online: true
oauth_config:
  redirect_urls:
    - <REDIRECT_URI_COPIED_FROM_COMPOSIO_AUTH_CONFIG>   # https only, exact value from the Composio dashboard
  scopes:
    bot:
      - app_mentions:read      # respond when someone @mentions the agent
      - chat:write             # post the agent's replies
      - im:history             # read DMs users send to the agent
      - channels:read          # let users pick a channel for output
      - users:read             # resolve user IDs to names in answers
      - channels:history       # read threads in public channels the bot was invited to
    bot_optional:
      - channels:history
    user:
      - search:read.public     # Real-time Search for the requesting user (needs Marketplace or internal app)
      - search:read.private
      - search:read.im
      - search:read.mpim
    user_optional:
      - search:read.private
      - search:read.im
      - search:read.mpim
settings:
  org_deploy_enabled: true       # org-ready for Enterprise customers; requires a bot scope
  socket_mode_enabled: false
  token_rotation_enabled: false  # set true ONLY if your token store refreshes Slack tokens; cannot be turned off later
artifacts.howToUse: Replace the placeholders, and paste the redirect URI exactly as the Composio auth-config dashboard shows it. Delete scopes for features you haven't shipped. Create the app at api.slack.com/apps -> Create New App -> From a manifest, then repeat with '-staging' in the name. The user search:read.* scopes only work once the app is internal or Marketplace-listed. For the Composio 'slack' (user-token) toolkit, add any user scopes its tools need, such as chat:write if the agent must post as the user.

artifacts.title: Scope justification text for the Marketplace submission
artifacts.content:
# Scope justifications for <YOUR_APP_NAME>
Paste each reason into the scope field of the Marketplace submission. Every reason names a shipped feature the reviewer can test. Delete rows for features you have not shipped.

| Scope | Token | Reason (how the app uses it) | How the reviewer can see it |
|---|---|---|---|
| app_mentions:read | bot | When a user types @<YOUR_APP_NAME> in a channel the bot was invited to, we read that one message to start an agent task and reply in the thread. | Mention the bot in #test with "summarize this thread". |
| chat:write | bot | We post the agent's answer as a threaded reply to the message that invoked it, and send task results to the user's DM with the app. | Same as above; the reply appears in the thread. |
| im:history | bot | Users chat with the agent in its Messages tab. We read only messages in that DM to continue the conversation. | Open the app's Messages tab and ask a question. |
| channels:history (optional) | bot | Only when a user invokes the agent inside a thread, we read that thread's messages so the answer has context. We do not crawl channels or store message content beyond the request (see retention below). | Mention the bot inside an existing thread. |
| channels:read | bot | The "Send results to" picker in App Home lists public channels so the user can choose where scheduled summaries go. | App Home -> Settings -> Send results to. |
| users:read | bot | We turn user IDs in retrieved messages into display names so answers say "Priya said..." instead of "U0123...". | Any answer that quotes a teammate. |
| search:read.public | user | When a user asks the agent a question, we call the Real-time Search API as that user to find relevant public-channel messages, and pass only the results to the model for that one answer. Nothing is indexed or stored. | Ask "What did we decide about the Q3 launch?" in the app's DM. |
| search:read.private / .im / .mpim (optional) | user | Same as above, but each user can opt in to include their own private channels and DMs. The agent can only see content the user can already see. | Re-authorize with the optional scopes and repeat the question. |

Retention statement (also in the privacy policy): message content returned by Slack is held in memory or a short-lived cache for at most <N minutes> to produce the answer and is then deleted. We store only IDs and metadata. Slack data is never used to train or fine-tune models. Model: <MODEL_NAME> via <PROVIDER>. Data tenancy: <single-tenant/multi-tenant>. Residency: <REGION>.
artifacts.howToUse: Paste one reason per scope into the submission form and keep the table in your reviewer notes. Edit the features, retention minutes, model, tenancy and region so they're true for your app; reviewers test what you claim.

artifacts.title: Slack Marketplace pre-submission checklist
artifacts.content:
# Pre-submission checklist: <YOUR_APP_NAME> -> Slack Marketplace

## Gate (submissions are blocked automatically if this fails)
- [ ] Installed on at least 10 active workspaces: real customer workspaces used in the last 28 days, not sandboxes. Stay at 10 or more during the whole review.
- [ ] Real usage on those workspaces. The guidelines call an app unsuitable when it has fewer than 10 active workspaces and fewer than 10 weekly active users.

## Suitability
- [ ] The agent has real in-Slack functionality (App Home, DM chat, mentions), not just an MCP or API bridge.
- [ ] No legacy or restricted scopes (search:read, admin.*, identity.*, triggers:*, workflow.steps:execute).
- [ ] No message export or backup, no bulk deletion, no auto-joining all public channels.
- [ ] Slack data is not used to train LLMs, and the privacy policy says so.

## Pages (public, no login)
- [ ] Landing page built for the Slack app: overview, how it works in Slack, install path, usage path, privacy link, and an AI-accuracy disclaimer.
- [ ] Support page with an email or form that needs no account. Response within 2 business days.
- [ ] Privacy policy covering what is collected, how it's used, retention, how to access, transfer or delete data, and a contact email or form.

## Listing
- [ ] Short description of 10 words or fewer. A long description that explains the problem and how the app works in Slack.
- [ ] High-resolution icon that doesn't resemble Slack or Slackbot.
- [ ] Images at 1600x1000 (8:5), .png/.jpg under 2 MB, showing the app in Slack.
- [ ] Optional: a public 30-90 s YouTube video with captions on and ads off.

## Submission form
- [ ] A reason for every scope (see the scope justification artifact), and the scope set matches what Composio requests.
- [ ] Test account(s) for <YOUR_PRODUCT>, with dummy data and a long trial. One per permission role.
- [ ] AI disclosures: model, retention and use, data tenancy, data residency.
- [ ] Demo video (encouraged, not required, and it speeds up review): full install and OAuth, setup, every feature, uninstall.
- [ ] Security contact email and phone. An architecture diagram (optional, but it speeds up review).
- [ ] A distributable staging app (<YOUR_APP_NAME>-staging) built from the same manifest.

## Technical
- [ ] HTTPS on every URL. No hard-coded tokens.
- [ ] The app handles missing optional scopes (missing_scope) and offers a re-authorize link.
- [ ] Post-OAuth domain check for enterprise customers. app_uninstalled cleanup deletes data within 14 business days.
- [ ] Notifications are opt-in. No @channel, no posting to #general by default, no emailing users without consent.
artifacts.howToUse: Work through it before clicking Submit, since every preliminary resubmission resets your queue position. Give the Pages section to whoever owns the website and legal text.

artifacts.title: Demo video script (install to uninstall)
artifacts.content:
# Demo video script: <YOUR_APP_NAME> (target 4-6 minutes, production app, realistic workspace)

1. 0:00 Intro (15 s): "This is <YOUR_APP_NAME>, an AI assistant from <YOUR_PRODUCT>. We'll install it, use every feature that needs a scope, then uninstall it."
2. 0:15 Install (45 s): Open the public landing page, click Add to Slack, and show the consent screen with the bot scopes, then the optional user search scopes. Approve. Show the post-install success page with next steps.
3. 1:00 Connect account (30 s): Show the onboarding message in App Home and click "Connect <YOUR_PRODUCT>". Sign in to the test account (the one supplied in the submission).
4. 1:30 DM chat (45 s): In the Messages tab, ask a question (im:history, chat:write). Show the "thinking" status and the answer with its AI disclaimer.
5. 2:15 Mention in a thread (45 s): In #project-x, @mention the bot inside a thread (app_mentions:read, channels:history). It replies in the thread and names teammates correctly (users:read).
6. 3:00 Search (60 s): Ask "What did we decide about pricing?" Point out that results come from Real-time Search as the user (search:read.public). Re-authorize with the optional DM scope and show a DM result appearing only for that user.
7. 4:00 Settings (30 s): App Home -> "Send results to" channel picker (channels:read). Show the support link and the pricing info.
8. 4:30 Missing scope (20 s): With an optional scope declined, show the graceful message and the re-authorize button.
9. 4:50 Uninstall (30 s): Remove the app from workspace settings. Show that the app_uninstalled cleanup ran (admin log or a confirmation email that the user opted in to).
10. 5:20 Close (10 s): Say how long data is retained, and that Slack data is never used for training.
artifacts.howToUse: Record it on the production app in a realistic workspace, not the dev app. Each numbered beat shows the scope(s) the reviewer needs to see in use. Upload it unlisted or public, and link it in the submission.

openQuestions: Are any existing installs of unlisted apps clamped in practice? Archived copies of Slack's own changelog and method page show the plan to clamp existing installs moving from 2 September 2025 to 3 March 2026 and then being dropped by 2 March 2026; current docs say existing installs are exempt. Third-party posts (allanninal.dev, a vendor post on dev.to) still describe enforcement from 3 March 2026, but none shows a test of an install made before 29 May 2025.

Would Slack judge an agent whose main interface is outside Slack (actions driven through Composio) as 'do not include functionality in Slack' and therefore unsuitable? The guidelines don't define the minimum in-Slack surface.

Real 2025-2026 review durations: beyond Slack's stated maximums, the only data points found are vendor-reported (2-3 months typical; one approval in 2 weeks after a viral launch that Salesforce prioritised). A Medium/gitconnected post reportedly describing about 4 months returned HTTP 403 and isn't cited.

The guidelines' unsuitable list pairs fewer than 10 active workspaces with fewer than 10 weekly active users. Do reviewers measure weekly active usage separately, beyond the automated 10-workspace submission gate?

When a customer independently creates an internal app in their own workspace and connects it to a third-party agent product, is that the customer's internal app or the vendor's 'Application template' under the API Terms? The terms address templates you provide but not customer-initiated setups.

Does Composio's managed Slack app actually fail on SLACK_ASSISTANT_SEARCH_CONTEXT (Real-time Search) today? This is inferred from Slack's rule that unlisted apps can't use RTS and wasn't tested, because no credentials were used.
Composio's documented callback URL for custom Slack auth configs wasn't verified here; always use the value its dashboard displays.
Is there a documented escalation path beyond the submission-flow feedback (for example a Marketplace team email) for disputed review decisions? None was found in the docs read.

Does the April 2026 AgentExchange merger change anything for Slack app developers (listing flow, fees, review)? Third-party posts say the process is unchanged, and Slack's developer docs don't mention AgentExchange yet.
